metadata.technology_specification: Benchtop flow cytometer with laser-based fluorescence detection
metadata.technology_reasoning: Benchtop flow cytometers with laser-based fluorescence detection are the most common form used in clinical and research laboratories due to their balance of complexity, size, and throughput. They dominate the market given the widespread use of fluorescent markers and laser excitation for multiparametric cell analysis as of 2024.

components.reasoning: The fluidics system is central to sample transport and hydrodynamic focusing, universally present as a major module in all flow cytometers.
This system is critical for excitation of fluorescent dyes and detection of emitted signals, always procured as separate laser modules, photomultiplier tubes, or photodiodes.
Includes the electronics for signal acquisition, amplification, and digitization, a standardized subsystem commonly integrated on dedicated circuit boards.
This assembly governs sample introduction into the fluidics stream, a distinct module essential in all designs though integration level varies slightly.
The flow cell is a precise microfluidic component where cells pass single file through the optical interrogation point, always a distinct replaceable part.

components.component: Data Acquisition and Analysis Software/Interface Module
components.reasoning: While software itself is not a physical component, the user interface hardware including control PC or embedded system is a common integral part.
The structural frame housing all subsystems, typically a separate manufactured assembly with standardized design for bench use.
